newsitem.title: FINLAND: Amer CEO sees profit in 1998.
newsitem.headline: Amer CEO sees profit in 1998.

text.p: Finnish sporting goods group Amer-yhtyma Oy's CEO Roger Talermo said on Friday he saw a "very fair chance" for the group to make a profit in 1998.
"I think we have a very fair chance to be in profitability already next year," Talermo told Reuters Financial Television (RFTV) in an interview.

Amer posted a 234 million markka loss before extraordinary items in 1996. On Thursday, releasing January-April results, it repeated that the group's full-year 1997 results would improve significantly but remain in the red.

Talermo, a former Finnish skiing champion, became president and CEO of Amer in May last year and under him the group has focused on sporting goods. He told RFTV sport equipment sales would make up "over 80 percent of our total business" in 1997.
"I think the main focus for the year to come is really to concentrate, and make the best business out of the sporting goods area where we have a lot of upside to make," he said.

"Our main strategical set-up is to carry a portfolio of sport equipment," he said, referring to Amer's product range covering summer and winter, indoor and outdoor as well as traditional and trend sports.
"This way we can better balance our global approach and certainly have areas where increases can be possible," he said.

In golf, which accounted for 31 percent of the sporting goods division's January-April sales, Talermo said Amer needed to regain market share as "we are not on the level where we should (be)". He did not elaborate.

Asked whether the other divisions, tobacco and time/systems, might be divested, he said: "Of course they are clearly not our focus ... It is not easy to sell the tobacco business where we are the licensed producer and we have a very long-lasting relationship with Philip Morris, I think it is a very good business for both sides."
In January-April, Amer Tobacco accounted for 10 percent of group net sales.
On Time/systems, with three percent of January-April sales, he said: "It is a very profitable business," but Amer was not ruling out making the most of any opportunities that may arise.
